results.summary_before: This SystemVerilog design is a fully combinational multiplier for 8-bit posit numbers with zero exponent bits. It decodes the two posit operands into fixed-point values and scale factors, aligns and multiplies them, then re-encodes the rounded product back into posit format. Operand A is supplied on the input pins, operand B on the bidirectional pins, and the product appears on the output pins. The design was exhaustively verified in simulation against a software reference before fabrication, and post-silicon testing is planned with a microcontroller or DIP switches; the description text mistakenly refers to a sum rather than a product.

results.summary_before: This design implements a quadratic sieve algorithm for factoring large integers, based on a pipeline architecture. It performs sieving operations over a factor base, updating a memory array and reporting when a threshold is exceeded. The chip interfaces via SPI and requires external SPI RAM for the sieve memory. Testing involves initializing the memory, running the sieve, and reading out addresses that likely factor completely. The design is notable for accelerating an integer factorization algorithm in hardware.

results.summary_before: This Verilog design reads the five channels of a BFD1000 infrared line-follower sensor plus clip and near obstacle signals, and produces left and right motor enable and direction outputs according to a set of logic equations. It also accepts proportional and integral gain values and a select signal on the bidirectional pins, and can take a PWM input for speed control. The design is tested by connecting the sensor to the input pins and the motor drivers to the outputs, with simulations run on a Nexys4 FPGA using Vivado. External hardware includes the BFD1000 sensor and two motor drivers with LED indicators, and the documentation provides a full truth table and the derived logic equations.

results.summary_before: This is a 4-digit passcode lock that unlocks only for the code 1010 and activates an alarm for 1111, with a wrong indicator for other codes. It is built from basic logic gates in Wokwi and is combinational, so outputs update directly with inputs. To test it, use DIP switches for the four inputs and observe three LEDs (unlock, wrong, alarm) and a buzzer. External hardware includes a DIP switch, three LEDs, and a buzzer. The design is intended for educational purposes and maps to Tiny Tapeout input/output blocks.

results.summary_before: This is a puzzle circuit based on the 'Holidays' Tiny Tapeout example, modified to allow exactly two holiday choices (or an extra sunscreen option). It takes eight inputs and one bidirectional input, and outputs a single logic signal that is true for only specific input combinations. The design is implemented in Wokwi. Testing requires setting the inputs to the specified patterns to get a true output. External hardware is just one LED for output. The documentation lists no other components.
